 Dengue fever is no longer seasonal; experts warn of new risks.
 More than 170,000 suspected cases of dengue fever have been recorded since the beginning of 2026. Experts warn that the disease occurs year-round, and the risk of transmission remains.
 Báo Lào Cai • 17/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 From the beginning of 2026 to the present, the whole country has recorded more than 170,000 suspected cases of dengue fever, including 21 deaths. According to experts, dengue fever now occurs year-round, instead of being concentrated seasonally as before.
 At Thanh Nhan Hospital, there are currently about 20 patients being treated for dengue fever. Dr. Nguyen Thu Huong, Head of the Occupational Diseases Department, Musculoskeletal Unit, and Head of the Infectious Diseases Unit at Thanh Nhan Hospital, said that the number of patients is trending downward compared to previous years but is still higher than the same period last year. Notably, the disease can become more complicated in people with underlying medical conditions.
 According to Dr. Huong, most cases of influenza and dengue fever requiring inpatient treatment are among children and the elderly, especially those with multiple underlying health conditions. Additionally, the disease is also seen in immunocompromised individuals, including cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy and radiation therapy, making treatment and care more complex.
 This was the third time the man had contracted dengue fever, and he had to be hospitalized. 
 Admitted to Thanh Nhan Hospital with symptoms of headache, fever of 38-39°C accompanied by dizziness and lightheadedness, 47-year-old NVK from Bach Mai ward, Hanoi, initially thought he had influenza A because a family member had been infected. After two days of self-treatment at home, he suddenly felt dizzy, fainted, and was quickly taken to the hospital about 15 minutes later.
 After the high fever subsided, Mr. K. told reporters that this was the third time he had contracted dengue fever. In previous instances, he had to be hospitalized due to the severity of the illness; however, this time he felt more tired and experienced a more prolonged headache. "In previous instances, my headache lessened after the fever subsided, but this time, even after the fever, the headache hasn't eased," Mr. K. shared. 
 Doctor Huong examines the patient. Regarding the patient's health status, Dr. Nguyen Thu Huong, a specialist in internal medicine, stated that the male patient was admitted to the hospital on the third day of his illness. Through examination and testing, doctors discovered that the patient had mild anemia, and his blood sodium level was significantly low, at only 120 mmol/L (normal range is 135-145 mmol/L).
 Doctors are currently investigating the cause of hyponatremia, raising the possibility that the patient may have paraneoplastic syndrome. According to Dr. Huong, this could be a case of discovering an underlying medical condition that had not been previously diagnosed during dengue fever treatment.
 According to People's Physician Professor Dr. Nguyen Van Kinh, former Director of the Central Hospital for Tropical Diseases, dengue fever has become an endemic disease in Vietnam. Previously, the disease usually appeared seasonally, especially in the South, with the number of cases often increasing during the rainy season. However, along with climate change, increased rainfall and prolonged rainy periods nationwide, the epidemiological situation of dengue fever has changed significantly.
 Previously, dengue fever typically occurred in certain months of the year, such as June to July or September to November. Now, however, the disease is recorded in all months. "Dengue fever has appeared year-round. This is a very significant disease burden," Professor Nguyen Van Kinh stated .
 Professor Nguyen Van Kinh stated that female mosquitoes infected with the Dengue virus can transmit the virus to their eggs, thereby forming new generations of mosquitoes. Therefore, even if a certain number of mosquitoes are eliminated, the mosquito population may still continue to exist.
 Besides environmental factors and the transmission characteristics of the virus, disease prevention and control at the grassroots level is also facing many difficulties. According to Professor Nguyen Van Kinh, in the past, community health and village health teams regularly carried out "door-to-door" monitoring to control disease vectors. Surveillance activities were also implemented through the Breteau index, which reflects the number of water containers with mosquito larvae per surveyed household.

 Regarding the course of the disease, Specialist Doctor Nguyen Thu Huong noted that during the first three days of dengue fever, patients mainly exhibit high fever. Treatment focuses on controlling body temperature, replenishing fluids and electrolytes, and ensuring adequate nutrition. When the temperature reaches 38.5°C or higher, patients should be given fever-reducing medication as directed by their doctor.
 However, from the fourth to the seventh day, even though the patient may no longer have a fever, this is a period with a high potential for complications. Notably, there may be thrombocytopenia, elevated liver enzymes, and increased vascular permeability, leading to fluid leakage in the pleura, peritoneum, and even the pericardium. For young people, doctors also pay particular attention to the risk of acute myocarditis caused by the Dengue virus. 
 Dengue fever occurs year-round. It represents a significant disease burden. Therefore, after being diagnosed with dengue fever by a doctor, patients need to follow the monitoring and treatment guidelines. During the first three days, fever control and fluid and electrolyte replacement are crucial. From the fourth day onwards, patients must be closely monitored at a medical facility. Even if there are no severe symptoms requiring hospitalization, patients should still go to a medical facility for daily tests and check-ups as directed.
 In particular, young children and the elderly are groups that need special attention. According to Dr. Huong, children have a higher fluid content in their bodies than adults, so when they become dehydrated, they are at a higher risk of dangerous complications. For the elderly, especially those with cardiovascular disease, dehydration can worsen their underlying conditions, increasing the risk of severe complications when they contract dengue fever.
 Dengue fever prevention and control must be carried out simultaneously and in a coordinated manner. 
 Given the fact that dengue fever occurs year-round, Professor Nguyen Van Kinh emphasized the role of epidemiological surveillance, early detection, and outbreak management.
 According to experts, the Department of Disease Prevention has developed software to support disease forecasting and warning. However, the most important thing remains detecting outbreaks in order to promptly implement control measures.
 In reality, dengue fever outbreaks can occur in different localities depending on the year. Some years Hanoi records outbreaks, while other years Ho Chi Minh City is the most affected. In 2024, a dengue fever outbreak occurred strongly in Hai Phong.
 According to Professor Nguyen Van Kinh, areas with heavy rainfall often have many puddles, creating favorable conditions for mosquitoes to lay eggs and increasing the risk of outbreaks. Therefore, monitoring, detection, containment, and treatment of outbreaks need to be carried out regularly to reduce the risk of people being bitten by disease-carrying mosquitoes.
 Experts also note that not all people infected with the Dengue virus show clinical symptoms. Although the body may develop immunity after infection, asymptomatic cases can easily lead to complacency, increasing the risk of transmission in the community. 
 From the fourth to the seventh day, even though the patient may no longer have a fever, this is a period with a high potential for complications. In particular, mosquito control efforts need to be implemented simultaneously throughout the entire residential area. Professor Nguyen Van Kinh explained that if one household sprays mosquito repellent but the neighboring house does not, when the insecticide wears off, mosquitoes from nearby areas can still fly over.
 You may also like Therefore, dengue prevention and control measures must be implemented simultaneously, synchronously, and comprehensively, instead of being implemented individually at the household level.
 Despite the difficulties, Professor Nguyen Van Kinh believes that dengue fever prevention and control also has certain advantages. In particular, Resolution 72 focuses on proactive disease prevention, creating conditions for investing resources in preventive medicine.
 According to experts, the Ministry of Health has decided to invest in groups carrying out dengue fever prevention and control work. This is something that those working in epidemic prevention and control have been waiting for.
 According to Professor Nguyen Van Kinh, there are three factors that contribute to the continued prevalence of dengue fever in Vietnam. Firstly, more than 90% of people infected with the dengue virus show no clinical symptoms. These individuals can still carry the virus in their bodies. When mosquitoes bite an infected person and then bite another person, the virus can continue to spread within the community.
 Secondly, completely eradicating mosquitoes and larvae is very difficult. As long as disease vectors remain, the risk of dengue transmission persists.
 Thirdly, changes in the environment, rainfall, and temperature create favorable conditions for mosquitoes to survive and thrive. In particular, rapid urbanization has led to the emergence of more areas where rainwater collects, becoming breeding grounds for Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes.
